Honesty isn&#x27;t optional.</p></div></article><article data-value-card="true" class="relative"><div data-slot="bracket"><div class="mb-2 flex items-baseline gap-2 whitespace-nowrap"><span class="relative inline-block"><span data-slot="number" class="font-misc text-primary text-sm">02</span><span class="font-misc text-primary absolute bottom-0 left-0 text-sm opacity-0">二</span></span><span class="font-misc text-primary text-sm opacity-0">[<!-- -->迅速<!-- -->]</span></div><div data-slot="bracket-line" class="border-primary h-3 w-full border-t border-r border-l"></div></div><div class="flex flex-col p-6 lg:p-8"><h3 class="text-title text-foreground text-glow w-fit text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl">URGENCY</h3><p class="text-paragraph text-muted-foreground mt-3 text-base">Move fast. Be impatient. Never settle for complacency or comfort. Speed is a feature.</p></div></article><article data-value-card="true" class="relative"><div data-slot="bracket"><div class="mb-2 flex items-baseline gap-2 whitespace-nowrap"><span class="relative inline-block"><span data-slot="number" class="font-misc text-primary text-sm">03</span><span class="font-misc text-primary absolute bottom-0 left-0 text-sm opacity-0">三</span></span><span class="font-misc text-primary text-sm opacity-0">[<!-- -->匠<!-- -->]</span></div><div data-slot="bracket-line" class="border-primary h-3 w-full border-t border-r border-l"></div></div><div class="flex flex-col p-6 lg:p-8"><h3 class="text-title text-foreground text-glow w-fit text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl">CRAFTSMANSHIP</h3><p class="text-paragraph text-muted-foreground mt-3 text-base">Take pride in your work. Care about design. Care about quality. Never ship garbage.</p></div></article><article data-value-card="true" class="relative"><div data-slot="bracket"><div class="mb-2 flex items-baseline gap-2 whitespace-nowrap"><span class="relative inline-block"><span data-slot="number" class="font-misc text-primary text-sm">04</span><span class="font-misc text-primary absolute bottom-0 left-0 text-sm opacity-0">四</span></span><span class="font-misc text-primary text-sm opacity-0">[<!-- -->貢献<!-- -->]</span></div><div data-slot="bracket-line" class="border-primary h-3 w-full border-t border-r border-l"></div></div><div class="flex flex-col p-6 lg:p-8"><h3 class="text-title text-foreground text-glow w-fit text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl">SERVICE</h3><p class="text-paragraph text-muted-foreground mt-3 text-base">Go above and beyond for customers. Extend that same care to teammates and partners. Service is everything.</p></div></article><article data-value-card="true" class="relative"><div data-slot="bracket"><div class="mb-2 flex items-baseline gap-2 whitespace-nowrap"><span class="relative inline-block"><span data-slot="number" class="font-misc text-primary text-sm">05</span><span class="font-misc text-primary absolute bottom-0 left-0 text-sm opacity-0">五</span></span><span class="font-misc text-primary text-sm opacity-0">[<!-- -->親切<!-- -->]</span></div><div data-slot="bracket-line" class="border-primary h-3 w-full border-t border-r border-l"></div></div><div class="flex flex-col p-6 lg:p-8"><h3 class="text-title text-foreground text-glow w-fit text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl">KINDNESS</h3><p class="text-paragraph text-muted-foreground mt-3 text-base">Be kind to everyone: teammates, customers, even competitors. Be direct, but always mindful. We&#x27;re all in this together.</p></div></article><article data-value-card="true" class="relative"><div data-slot="bracket"><div class="mb-2 flex items-baseline gap-2 whitespace-nowrap"><span class="relative inline-block"><span data-slot="number" class="font-misc text-primary text-sm">06</span><span class="font-misc text-primary absolute bottom-0 left-0 text-sm opacity-0">六</span></span><span class="font-misc text-primary text-sm opacity-0">[<!-- -->遊び心<!-- -->]</span></div><div data-slot="bracket-line" class="border-primary h-3 w-full border-t border-r border-l"></div></div><div class="flex flex-col p-6 lg:p-8"><h3 class="text-title text-foreground text-glow w-fit text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl">FUN</h3><p class="text-paragraph text-muted-foreground mt-3 text-base">Enjoy the work. Enjoy each other. Do things because they&#x27;re cool. Smile through the pain.</p></div></article></div></div></div></section><section data-section="about-mission-vision" class="relative"><!--$!--><template data-dgst="BAILOUT_TO_CLIENT_SIDE_RENDERING"></template><!--/$--><div class="container-responsive space-y-20 py-40 md:space-y-40 md:py-56"><div data-slot="about-vision" class=""><div class="flex max-w-[85ch] flex-col text-pretty max-sm:mt-8 items-start" data-text-block="true"><span class="font-misc inline-flex items-center rounded-sm uppercase transition-colors-and-shadows px-1 py-0.5 pt-0.75 border border-primary text-primary text-sm leading-[0.9] mb-4" data-badge="true">ORIGINS</span><p class="text-paragraph text-muted text-[22px] leading-[1.3] tracking-tight text-balance max-md:text-pretty md:text-4xl " data-text-content="true">Our team spent years in account supply and media buying before building<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">the market</strong>. We saw how much launch speed depends on access — teams move fast when they have the right resource. But we also witnessed firsthand the<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">challenges and complexity</strong>. The chat hunting. The bad supply. The launches delayed by unreliable sellers.</p></div></div><div data-slot="about-founder" class="flex justify-end"><div class="flex max-w-[85ch] flex-col text-pretty max-sm:mt-8 items-end" data-text-block="true"><span class="font-misc inline-flex items-center rounded-sm uppercase transition-colors-and-shadows px-1 py-0.5 pt-0.75 border border-primary text-primary text-sm leading-[0.9] mb-4" data-badge="true">SPARK</span><p class="text-paragraph text-muted text-[22px] leading-[1.3] tracking-tight text-balance max-md:text-pretty md:text-4xl text-right" data-text-content="true">Over five years in the market, we built<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">a reliable supply channel</strong> <!-- -->for teams running traffic at scale. But account supply still felt painfully chaotic, <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">stuck in Telegram noise</strong>. That&#x27;s when it clicked: if AI can write code, why can&#x27;t it understand production?</p></div></div><div data-slot="about-history" class=""><div class="flex max-w-[85ch] flex-col text-pretty max-sm:mt-8 items-start" data-text-block="true"><span class="font-misc inline-flex items-center rounded-sm uppercase transition-colors-and-shadows px-1 py-0.5 pt-0.75 border border-primary text-primary text-sm leading-[0.9] mb-4" data-badge="true">MISSION</span><p class="text-paragraph text-muted text-[22px] leading-[1.3] tracking-tight text-balance max-md:text-pretty md:text-4xl " data-text-content="true">To become the<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">default access channel</strong> for media buying teams that need speed and stability. Structured access infrastructure — clear, fast, and built for teams who launch.</p></div></div><div data-slot="about-mission" class="flex justify-end"><div class="flex max-w-[85ch] flex-col text-pretty max-sm:mt-8 items-end" data-text-block="true"><span class="font-misc inline-flex items-center rounded-sm uppercase transition-colors-and-shadows px-1 py-0.5 pt-0.75 border border-primary text-primary text-sm leading-[0.9] mb-4" data-badge="true">VISION</span><p class="text-paragraph text-muted text-[22px] leading-[1.3] tracking-tight text-balance max-md:text-pretty md:text-4xl text-right" data-text-content="true">A world where<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">teams launch without hunting for access</strong> <!-- -->without human intervention or direction. Where systems understand their own health, diagnose their own issues, and fix their own bugs. Where engineers spend their time building, not firefighting.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="py-section bg-background"><div class="container-responsive relative"><div class="hidden Smile through the pain.</p></div></article></div></div></div></section><section data-section="about-mission-vision" class="relative"><!--$!--><template data-dgst="BAILOUT_TO_CLIENT_SIDE_RENDERING"></template><!--/$--><div class="container-responsive space-y-20 py-40 md:space-y-40 md:py-56"><div data-slot="about-vision" class=""><div class="flex max-w-[85ch] flex-col text-pretty max-sm:mt-8 items-start" data-text-block="true"><span class="font-misc inline-flex items-center rounded-sm uppercase transition-colors-and-shadows px-1 py-0.5 pt-0.75 border border-primary text-primary text-sm leading-[0.9] mb-4" data-badge="true">ORIGINS</span><p class="text-paragraph text-muted text-[22px] leading-[1.3] tracking-tight text-balance max-md:text-pretty md:text-4xl " data-text-content="true">Our team spent years in account supply and media buying before building<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">the market</strong>. We saw how much launch speed depends on access — teams move fast when they have the right resource. But we also witnessed firsthand the<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">challenges and complexity</strong>. The chat hunting. The bad supply. The launches delayed by unreliable sellers.</p></div></div><div data-slot="about-founder" class="flex justify-end"><div class="flex max-w-[85ch] flex-col text-pretty max-sm:mt-8 items-end" data-text-block="true"><span class="font-misc inline-flex items-center rounded-sm uppercase transition-colors-and-shadows px-1 py-0.5 pt-0.75 border border-primary text-primary text-sm leading-[0.9] mb-4" data-badge="true">SPARK</span><p class="text-paragraph text-muted text-[22px] leading-[1.3] tracking-tight text-balance max-md:text-pretty md:text-4xl text-right" data-text-content="true">Over five years in the market, we built<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">a reliable supply channel</strong> <!-- -->for teams running traffic at scale. But account supply still felt painfully chaotic, <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">stuck in Telegram noise</strong>. That&#x27;s when it clicked: if AI can write code, why can&#x27;t it understand production?</p></div></div><div data-slot="about-history" class=""><div class="flex max-w-[85ch] flex-col text-pretty max-sm:mt-8 items-start" data-text-block="true"><span class="font-misc inline-flex items-center rounded-sm uppercase transition-colors-and-shadows px-1 py-0.5 pt-0.75 border border-primary text-primary text-sm leading-[0.9] mb-4" data-badge="true">MISSION</span><p class="text-paragraph text-muted text-[22px] leading-[1.3] tracking-tight text-balance max-md:text-pretty md:text-4xl " data-text-content="true">To become the<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">default access channel</strong> for media buying teams that need speed and stability. Structured access infrastructure — clear, fast, and built for teams who launch.</p></div></div><div data-slot="about-mission" class="flex justify-end"><div class="flex max-w-[85ch] flex-col text-pretty max-sm:mt-8 items-end" data-text-block="true"><span class="font-misc inline-flex items-center rounded-sm uppercase transition-colors-and-shadows px-1 py-0.5 pt-0.75 border border-primary text-primary text-sm leading-[0.9] mb-4" data-badge="true">VISION</span><p class="text-paragraph text-muted text-[22px] leading-[1.3] tracking-tight text-balance max-md:text-pretty md:text-4xl text-right" data-text-content="true">A world where<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">teams launch without hunting for access</strong> <!-- -->without human intervention or direction. Where systems understand their own health, diagnose their own issues, and fix their own bugs. Where engineers spend their time building, not firefighting.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="py-section bg-background"><div class="container-responsive relative"><div class="hidden These six principles are the foundation of how we build impact.accs.</p></div><div class="mx-auto mt-16 grid max-w-6xl grid-cols-1 gap-x-16 text-left max-lg:gap-y-4 lg:grid-cols-2"><article data-value-card="true" class="relative"><div data-slot="bracket"><div class="mb-2 flex items-baseline gap-2 whitespace-nowrap"><span class="relative inline-block"><span data-slot="number" class="font-misc text-primary text-sm">01</span><span class="font-misc text-primary absolute bottom-0 left-0 text-sm opacity-0">一</span></span><span class="font-misc text-primary text-sm opacity-0">[<!-- -->誠実<!-- -->]</span></div><div data-slot="bracket-line" class="border-primary h-3 w-full border-t border-r border-l"></div></div><div class="flex flex-col p-6 lg:p-8"><h3 class="text-title text-foreground text-glow w-fit text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl">INTEGRITY</h3><p class="text-paragraph text-muted-foreground mt-3 text-base">Do the right thing, always. By our customers, Team Lead, our investors. Honesty isn&#x27;t optional.</p></div></article><article data-value-card="true" class="relative"><div data-slot="bracket"><div class="mb-2 flex items-baseline gap-2 whitespace-nowrap"><span class="relative inline-block"><span data-slot="number" class="font-misc text-primary text-sm">02</span><span class="font-misc text-primary absolute bottom-0 left-0 text-sm opacity-0">二</span></span><span class="font-misc text-primary text-sm opacity-0">[<!-- -->迅速<!-- -->]</span></div><div data-slot="bracket-line" class="border-primary h-3 w-full border-t border-r border-l"></div></div><div class="flex flex-col p-6 lg:p-8"><h3 class="text-title text-foreground text-glow w-fit text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl">URGENCY</h3><p class="text-paragraph text-muted-foreground mt-3 text-base">Move fast. Be impatient. Never settle for complacency or comfort. Speed is a feature.</p></div></article><article data-value-card="true" class="relative"><div data-slot="bracket"><div class="mb-2 flex items-baseline gap-2 whitespace-nowrap"><span class="relative inline-block"><span data-slot="number" class="font-misc text-primary text-sm">03</span><span class="font-misc text-primary absolute bottom-0 left-0 text-sm opacity-0">三</span></span><span class="font-misc text-primary text-sm opacity-0">[<!-- -->匠<!-- -->]</span></div><div data-slot="bracket-line" class="border-primary h-3 w-full border-t border-r border-l"></div></div><div class="flex flex-col p-6 lg:p-8"><h3 class="text-title text-foreground text-glow w-fit text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl">CRAFTSMANSHIP</h3><p class="text-paragraph text-muted-foreground mt-3 text-base">Take pride in your work. Care about design. Care about quality. Never ship garbage.</p></div></article><article data-value-card="true" class="relative"><div data-slot="bracket"><div class="mb-2 flex items-baseline gap-2 whitespace-nowrap"><span class="relative inline-block"><span data-slot="number" class="font-misc text-primary text-sm">04</span><span class="font-misc text-primary absolute bottom-0 left-0 text-sm opacity-0">四</span></span><span class="font-misc text-primary text-sm opacity-0">[<!-- -->貢献<!-- -->]</span></div><div data-slot="bracket-line" class="border-primary h-3 w-full border-t border-r border-l"></div></div><div class="flex flex-col p-6 lg:p-8"><h3 class="text-title text-foreground text-glow w-fit text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl">SERVICE</h3><p class="text-paragraph text-muted-foreground mt-3 text-base">Go above and beyond for customers. Extend that same care to teammates and partners. Service is everything.</p></div></article><article data-value-card="true" class="relative"><div data-slot="bracket"><div class="mb-2 flex items-baseline gap-2 whitespace-nowrap"><span class="relative inline-block"><span data-slot="number" class="font-misc text-primary text-sm">05</span><span class="font-misc text-primary absolute bottom-0 left-0 text-sm opacity-0">五</span></span><span class="font-misc text-primary text-sm opacity-0">[<!-- -->親切<!-- -->]</span></div><div data-slot="bracket-line" class="border-primary h-3 w-full border-t border-r border-l"></div></div><div class="flex flex-col p-6 lg:p-8"><h3 class="text-title text-foreground text-glow w-fit text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl">KINDNESS</h3><p class="text-paragraph text-muted-foreground mt-3 text-base">Be kind to everyone: teammates, customers, even competitors. Be direct, but always mindful. We&#x27;re all in this together.</p></div></article><article data-value-card="true" class="relative"><div data-slot="bracket"><div class="mb-2 flex items-baseline gap-2 whitespace-nowrap"><span class="relative inline-block"><span data-slot="number" class="font-misc text-primary text-sm">06</span><span class="font-misc text-primary absolute bottom-0 left-0 text-sm opacity-0">六</span></span><span class="font-misc text-primary text-sm opacity-0">[<!-- -->遊び心<!-- -->]</span></div><div data-slot="bracket-line" class="border-primary h-3 w-full border-t border-r border-l"></div></div><div class="flex flex-col p-6 lg:p-8"><h3 class="text-title text-foreground text-glow w-fit text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl">FUN</h3><p class="text-paragraph text-muted-foreground mt-3 text-base">Enjoy the work. Enjoy each other. Do things because they&#x27;re cool. Smile through the pain.</p></div></article></div></div></div></section><section data-section="about-mission-vision" class="relative"><!--$!--><template data-dgst="BAILOUT_TO_CLIENT_SIDE_RENDERING"></template><!--/$--><div class="container-responsive space-y-20 py-40 md:space-y-40 md:py-56"><div data-slot="about-vision" class=""><div class="flex max-w-[85ch] flex-col text-pretty max-sm:mt-8 items-start" data-text-block="true"><span class="font-misc inline-flex items-center rounded-sm uppercase transition-colors-and-shadows px-1 py-0.5 pt-0.75 border border-primary text-primary text-sm leading-[0.9] mb-4" data-badge="true">ORIGINS</span><p class="text-paragraph text-muted text-[22px] leading-[1.3] tracking-tight text-balance max-md:text-pretty md:text-4xl " data-text-content="true">Our team spent years in account supply and media buying before building<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">the market</strong>. We saw how much launch speed depends on access — teams move fast when they have the right resource. But we also witnessed firsthand the<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">challenges and complexity</strong>. The chat hunting. The bad supply. The launches delayed by unreliable sellers.</p></div></div><div data-slot="about-founder" class="flex justify-end"><div class="flex max-w-[85ch] flex-col text-pretty max-sm:mt-8 items-end" data-text-block="true"><span class="font-misc inline-flex items-center rounded-sm uppercase transition-colors-and-shadows px-1 py-0.5 pt-0.75 border border-primary text-primary text-sm leading-[0.9] mb-4" data-badge="true">SPARK</span><p class="text-paragraph text-muted text-[22px] leading-[1.3] tracking-tight text-balance max-md:text-pretty md:text-4xl text-right" data-text-content="true">Over five years in the market, we built<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">a reliable supply channel</strong> <!-- -->for teams running traffic at scale. But account supply still felt painfully chaotic, <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">stuck in Telegram noise</strong>. That&#x27;s when it clicked: if AI can write code, why can&#x27;t it understand production?</p></div></div><div data-slot="about-history" class=""><div class="flex max-w-[85ch] flex-col text-pretty max-sm:mt-8 items-start" data-text-block="true"><span class="font-misc inline-flex items-center rounded-sm uppercase transition-colors-and-shadows px-1 py-0.5 pt-0.75 border border-primary text-primary text-sm leading-[0.9] mb-4" data-badge="true">MISSION</span><p class="text-paragraph text-muted text-[22px] leading-[1.3] tracking-tight text-balance max-md:text-pretty md:text-4xl " data-text-content="true">To become the<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">default access channel</strong> for media buying teams that need speed and stability. Structured access infrastructure — clear, fast, and built for teams who launch.</p></div></div><div data-slot="about-mission" class="flex justify-end"><div class="flex max-w-[85ch] flex-col text-pretty max-sm:mt-8 items-end" data-text-block="true"><span class="font-misc inline-flex items-center rounded-sm uppercase transition-colors-and-shadows px-1 py-0.5 pt-0.75 border border-primary text-primary text-sm leading-[0.9] mb-4" data-badge="true">VISION</span><p class="text-paragraph text-muted text-[22px] leading-[1.3] tracking-tight text-balance max-md:text-pretty md:text-4xl text-right" data-text-content="true">A world where<!-- --> <strong class="text-card-foreground text-glow font-medium">teams launch without hunting for access</strong> <!-- -->without human intervention or direction. Where systems understand their own health, diagnose their own issues, and fix their own bugs. Where engineers spend their time building, not firefighting.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="py-section bg-background"><div class="container-responsive relative"><div class="hidden 539: 
540: 
541: <p>We may also process Personal Information of our Clients’ visitors and customers, and visitors to our Clients’ websites (or our Client’s application downloads) in performance of the Services on behalf of our Clients. In this context we are a “service provider” or “data processor” (as those terms are defined by applicable laws). This Personal Information may consist of Internet Protocol (“IP”) addresses, account or membership numbers (without a key to personally identify you), and/or email addresses, although, if it is our Clients sending email addresses to us, we request that our Clients encrypt email addresses prior to sending to us. We take security measures to protect all Personal Information, including by hashing IP addresses and further encrypting email addresses. We do not associate Personal Information with individuals and are subject to our Clients’ instructions regarding such collection and use of such Personal Information. As a vendor of our Clients, the bases for our collection and processing of Personal Information of their customers and visitors may be through consent obtained by our Client, our Client’s legitimate interests, or (in accordance with applicable law) a lawful business purpose.</p>
542: 
543: 
```

```text
581: 
582: 
583: <p>If you are a customer of one of our Clients, or a visitor to their website (or have downloaded one of our Client’s applications), please contact the Client to request access to your Personal Information, or to correct or have such information deleted. If you do contact Impact, Impact does not associate the data that we process on behalf of our Clients with any particular individual, and Impact may not be able to verify whether we have Personal Information that belongs to you. See information below at How to Contact Us if you have questions regarding this policy or requests regarding your Personal Information.</p>
584: 
585:

```text
593: 
594: 
595: <p>The Log Data that we collect for our Clients, of visitors to their website or mobile applications, includes the visitor’s computer or mobile device IP address, browser type, browser version, and the ads that you interact with. If you are referred by one of our Clients to another’s website or application from interactions with the ads, we are passed information if you conclude an action there, such as the purchase of goods or services, signing-up for a newsletter or downloading an application. Impact does not receive your name, address, credit card, or other personally identifying information.</p>
596: 
597:

677: 
678: 
679: <p>Analytics &amp; Services. Impact uses information for analytics to understand how our Services are used, as well as in the performance of our Services. We disclose data to our Clients pursuant to our agreements with them and their instructions, and this includes Personal Data of visitors to their websites and applications. If instructed by a Client to delete Personal Data, we delete the data or anonymized it (including automatically after a set period of time).</p>
680: 
681: 
```

```text
709: 
710: 
711: <p>When deleting data, the Personal Data is completely removed from our servers or retained only in anonymized form. If we have collected Personal Data about you from more than one Client, we will delete all instances of the Personal Data that we have at the time of the request (to the extent that we are able to verify and match such data). However, if you subsequently authorize or visit the same Client or another Client’s website or application, we will have processed your Personal Data in relation to such authorization or visit.</p>
712:

142: <p>To increase the efficiency of administration and resolution of arbitrations, you and Company agree that in the event that there are 100 or more individual Requests of a substantially similar nature filed against Company by or with the assistance of the same law firm, group of law firms, or organizations, within a 30-day period (or as soon as possible thereafter), the JAMS shall (1) administer the arbitration demands in batches of 100 Requests per batch (plus, to the extent there are less than 100 Requests left over after the batching described above, a final batch consisting of the remaining Requests); (2) appoint one arbitrator for each batch; and (3) provide for the resolution of each batch as a single consolidated arbitration with one set of filing and administrative fees due per side per batch, one procedural calendar, one hearing (if any) in a place to be determined by the arbitrator, and one final award (&quot;Batch Arbitration&quot;).</p>
143: <p>All parties agree that Requests are of a &quot;substantially similar nature&quot; if they arise out of or relate to the same event or factual scenario and raise the same or similar legal issues and seek the same or similar relief. To the extent the parties disagree on the application of the Batch Arbitration process, the disagreeing party shall advise the JAMS, and the JAMS shall appoint a sole standing arbitrator to determine the applicability of the Batch Arbitration process (&quot;Administrative Arbitrator&quot;). In an effort to expedite resolution of any such dispute by the Administrative Arbitrator, the parties agree the Administrative Arbitrator may set forth such procedures as are necessary to resolve any disputes promptly. The Administrative Arbitrator&#x27;s fees shall be paid by Company.</p>
144: <p>You and Company agree to cooperate in good faith with the JAMS to implement the Batch Arbitration process including the payment of single filing and administrative fees for batches of Requests, as well as any steps to minimize the time and costs of arbitration, which may include: (1) the appointment of a discovery special master to assist the arbitrator in the resolution of discovery disputes; and (2) the adoption of an expedited calendar of the arbitration proceedings.</p>
145: <p>This Batch Arbitration provision shall in no way be interpreted as authorizing a class, collective and/or mass arbitration or action of any kind, or arbitration involving joint or consolidated claims under any circumstances, except as expressly set forth in this provision.</p>

141: <h4 id="h-batch-arbitration"><a href="#h-batch-arbitration" class="group block no-underline">(h) Batch Arbitration<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-link mb-1 ml-2 inline-block size-[0.6em] opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-50" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M10 13a5 5 0 0 0 7.54.54l3-3a5 5 0 0 0-7.07-7.07l-1.72 1.71"></path><path d="M14 11a5 5 0 0 0-7.54-.54l-3 3a5 5 0 0 0 7.07 7.07l1.71-1.71"></path></svg></a></h4>
142: <p>To increase the efficiency of administration and resolution of arbitrations, you and Company agree that in the event that there are 100 or more individual Requests of a substantially similar nature filed against Company by or with the assistance of the same law firm, group of law firms, or organizations, within a 30-day period (or as soon as possible thereafter), the JAMS shall (1) administer the arbitration demands in batches of 100 Requests per batch (plus, to the extent there are less than 100 Requests left over after the batching described above, a final batch consisting of the remaining Requests); (2) appoint one arbitrator for each batch; and (3) provide for the resolution of each batch as a single consolidated arbitration with one set of filing and administrative fees due per side per batch, one procedural calendar, one hearing (if any) in a place to be determined by the arbitrator, and one final award (&quot;Batch Arbitration&quot;).</p>
143: <p>All parties agree that Requests are of a &quot;substantially similar nature&quot; if they arise out of or relate to the same event or factual scenario and raise the same or similar legal issues and seek the same or similar relief. To the extent the parties disagree on the application of the Batch Arbitration process, the disagreeing party shall advise the JAMS, and the JAMS shall appoint a sole standing arbitrator to determine the applicability of the Batch Arbitration process (&quot;Administrative Arbitrator&quot;). In an effort to expedite resolution of any such dispute by the Administrative Arbitrator, the parties agree the Administrative Arbitrator may set forth such procedures as are necessary to resolve any disputes promptly. The Administrative Arbitrator&#x27;s fees shall be paid by Company.</p>
144: <p>You and Company agree to cooperate in good faith with the JAMS to implement the Batch Arbitration process including the payment of single filing and administrative fees for batches of Requests, as well as any steps to minimize the time and costs of arbitration, which may include: (1) the appointment of a discovery special master to assist the arbitrator in the resolution of discovery disputes; and (2) the adoption of an expedited calendar of the arbitration proceedings.</p>
145: <p>This Batch Arbitration provision shall in no way be interpreted as authorizing a class, collective and/or mass arbitration or action of any kind, or arbitration involving joint or consolidated claims under any circumstances, except as expressly set forth in this provision.</p>

141: <h4 id="h-batch-arbitration"><a href="#h-batch-arbitration" class="group block no-underline">(h) Batch Arbitration<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-link mb-1 ml-2 inline-block size-[0.6em] opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-50" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M10 13a5 5 0 0 0 7.54.54l3-3a5 5 0 0 0-7.07-7.07l-1.72 1.71"></path><path d="M14 11a5 5 0 0 0-7.54-.54l-3 3a5 5 0 0 0 7.07 7.07l1.71-1.71"></path></svg></a></h4>
142: <p>To increase the efficiency of administration and resolution of arbitrations, you and Company agree that in the event that there are 100 or more individual Requests of a substantially similar nature filed against Company by or with the assistance of the same law firm, group of law firms, or organizations, within a 30-day period (or as soon as possible thereafter), the JAMS shall (1) administer the arbitration demands in batches of 100 Requests per batch (plus, to the extent there are less than 100 Requests left over after the batching described above, a final batch consisting of the remaining Requests); (2) appoint one arbitrator for each batch; and (3) provide for the resolution of each batch as a single consolidated arbitration with one set of filing and administrative fees due per side per batch, one procedural calendar, one hearing (if any) in a place to be determined by the arbitrator, and one final award (&quot;Batch Arbitration&quot;).</p>
143: <p>All parties agree that Requests are of a &quot;substantially similar nature&quot; if they arise out of or relate to the same event or factual scenario and raise the same or similar legal issues and seek the same or similar relief. To the extent the parties disagree on the application of the Batch Arbitration process, the disagreeing party shall advise the JAMS, and the JAMS shall appoint a sole standing arbitrator to determine the applicability of the Batch Arbitration process (&quot;Administrative Arbitrator&quot;). In an effort to expedite resolution of any such dispute by the Administrative Arbitrator, the parties agree the Administrative Arbitrator may set forth such procedures as are necessary to resolve any disputes promptly. The Administrative Arbitrator&#x27;s fees shall be paid by Company.</p>
144: <p>You and Company agree to cooperate in good faith with the JAMS to implement the Batch Arbitration process including the payment of single filing and administrative fees for batches of Requests, as well as any steps to minimize the time and costs of arbitration, which may include: (1) the appointment of a discovery special master to assist the arbitrator in the resolution of discovery disputes; and (2) the adoption of an expedited calendar of the arbitration proceedings.</p>
145: <p>This Batch Arbitration provision shall in no way be interpreted as authorizing a class, collective and/or mass arbitration or action of any kind, or arbitration involving joint or consolidated claims under any circumstances, except as expressly set forth in this provision.</p>

Incident responders are flooded with information during high-stress situations.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Observability vendors promised clarity. What we got was complexity.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"The DevOps movement gained traction around a simple idea: the people who build software should also operate it. But observability tools aren&#x27;t built for product engineers. They are designed for platform specialists with deep expertise in infrastructure, databases, and distributed systems. This is unfair.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Product engineers don&#x27;t want more observability bells and whistles. Flame graphs look sophisticated but are unintuitive for most people.\"}]\n35:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Logs are different.\"}]\n36:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Everyone knows how to write a log line. Less is More\",[\"$\",\"$L31\",null,{\"ref\":\"$undefined\",\"iconNode\":[[\"path\",{\"d\":\"M10 13a5 5 0 0 0 7.54.54l3-3a5 5 0 0 0-7.07-7.07l-1.72 1.71\",\"key\":\"1cjeqo\"}],[\"path\",{\"d\":\"M14 11a5 5 0 0 0-7.54-.54l-3 3a5 5 0 0 0 7.07 7.07l1.71-1.71\",\"key\":\"19qd67\"}]],\"className\":\"lucide-link mb-1 ml-2 inline-block size-[0.6em] opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-50\",\"aria-hidden\":\"true\"}]]}]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Modern observability is bloated.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Over the past decade, observability platforms have accumulated hundreds of features, modules, dashboards, and configuration options. While these elements look impressive in demos, they rarely lead to more reliable systems. More often, they do the opposite by creating a steep learning curve and increasing cognitive load.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"The cost is felt everywhere. Junior engineers struggle to make sense of sprawling UIs. Non-technical teammates are effectively locked out, unable to answer basic questions about production. Incident responders are flooded with information during high-stress situations.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Observability vendors promised clarity. What we got was complexity.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"The DevOps movement gained traction around a simple idea: the people who build software should also operate it. But observability tools aren&#x27;t built for product engineers. They are designed for platform specialists with deep expertise in infrastructure, databases, and distributed systems. This is unfair.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Product engineers don&#x27;t want more observability bells and whistles. They want answers:\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"ul\",null,{\"children\":[\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"Why is production down?\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"Who is affected?\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"What changed?\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"How do we fix it right now?\"}],\"\\n\"]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"And if observability is fundamentally about answering questions, it follows that the best UI for observability is chat.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"We don&#x27;t make observability better by adding more features. We make it better by cutting back.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":[\"$\",\"strong\",null,{\"children\":\"Less is more.\"}]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"h2\",null,{\"id\":\"2-logs-are-all-you-need\",\"children\":[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"#2-logs-are-all-you-need\",\"className\":\"group block no-underline\",\"children\":[\"2. The belief is that all three are required to understand production systems.\"}]\n33:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"This idea is outdated.\"}]\n34:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Metrics and traces are powerful in theory but brittle in practice. Instrumentation is complex and error-prone. Aggregations are confusing and often hide real problems. Flame graphs look sophisticated but are unintuitive for most people.\"}]\n35:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Logs are different.\"}]\n36:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Everyone knows how to write a log line. Everyone knows how to read stdout. Logs match how humans naturally reason about systems: what happened, in what order, and with what context.\"}]\n37:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"On a fundamental level, logs, metrics, and traces share the same underlying DNA: events. Metrics are aggregated events. Traces are collections of start and end events. Logs are events masquerading under a different name. The implications of this are profound: with logs, you can reconstruct metrics and traces, giving you three \\\"pillars\\\" for the price of one.\"}]\n38:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Historically, logs were dismissed because they were unstructured. Today, that weakness is a strength. AI excels at processing large volumes of unstructured text. It can surface patterns, identify anomalies, and extract meaning from natural language at scale. Metrics and traces could never hope to be as rich.\"}]\n39:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Logs have challenges, too. Cost and availability are chief among them. But these aren't insurmountable. Cost can be addressed with summarization, compression, tiering, and intelligent retention. Availability can be improved through automatic instrumentation: AI that adds meaningful log lines directly to code.\"}]\n3a:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"The Bitter Lesson taught us that AI progress doesn't come from clever hacks. It comes from simple, scalable primitives. Observability is about understanding: the ability to explore systems and explain failures.\"}]\n3e:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Today, software teams think of monitoring as a necessary evil — a painful but essential part of running production systems. But this consensus doesn't change the truth: monitoring is fundamentally broken.\"}]\n3f:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Ask any engineer, and you'll hear the same complaints:\"}]\n40:[\"$\",\"ul\",null,{\"children\":[\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"Monitors are tedious to create and maintain.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"They require constant tuning.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"They misfire.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"They page the wrong people at the wrong time.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"Worst of all, they train teams to ignore alerts that sometimes represent real customer pain.\"}],\"\\n\"]}]\n41:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"These tradeoffs might be acceptable if monitors reliably caught issues. They don't.\"}]\n42:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Monitoring fails because it's reactive. Teams create monitors after incidents, not before. Meanwhile, the systems they manage are complex, constantly changing, and rarely fail the same way twice.\"}]\n43:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"We're playing a losing game. We don't need better monitors. Yet the tools we use to understand them are still rooted in assumptions from a bygone era.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Something has to change. This manifesto lays out a path forward.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"h2\",null,{\"id\":\"1-less-is-more\",\"children\":[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"#1-less-is-more\",\"className\":\"group block no-underline\",\"children\":[\"1. Less is More\",[\"$\",\"$L31\",null,{\"ref\":\"$undefined\",\"iconNode\":[[\"path\",{\"d\":\"M10 13a5 5 0 0 0 7.54.54l3-3a5 5 0 0 0-7.07-7.07l-1.72 1.71\",\"key\":\"1cjeqo\"}],[\"path\",{\"d\":\"M14 11a5 5 0 0 0-7.54-.54l-3 3a5 5 0 0 0 7.07 7.07l1.71-1.71\",\"key\":\"19qd67\"}]],\"className\":\"lucide-link mb-1 ml-2 inline-block size-[0.6em] opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-50\",\"aria-hidden\":\"true\"}]]}]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Modern observability is bloated.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Over the past decade, observability platforms have accumulated hundreds of features, modules, dashboards, and configuration options. While these elements look impressive in demos, they rarely lead to more reliable systems. More often, they do the opposite by creating a steep learning curve and increasing cognitive load.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"The cost is felt everywhere. Junior engineers struggle to make sense of sprawling UIs. Non-technical teammates are effectively locked out, unable to answer basic questions about production. Incident responders are flooded with information during high-stress situations.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Observability vendors promised clarity. What we got was complexity.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"The DevOps movement gained traction around a simple idea: the people who build software should also operate it. But observability tools aren&#x27;t built for product engineers. They are designed for platform specialists with deep expertise in infrastructure, databases, and distributed systems. This is unfair.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Product engineers don&#x27;t want more observability bells and whistles. They want answers:\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"ul\",null,{\"children\":[\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"Why is production down?\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"Who is affected?\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"What changed?\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"How do we fix it right now?\"}],\"\\n\"]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"And if observability is fundamentally about answering questions, it follows that the best UI for observability is chat.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"We don&#x27;t make observability better by adding more features. We make it better by cutting back.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":[\"$\",\"strong\",null,{\"children\":\"Less is more.\"}]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"h2\",null,{\"id\":\"2-logs-are-all-you-need\",\"children\":[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"#2-logs-are-all-you-need\",\"className\":\"group block no-underline\",\"children\":[\"2. The belief is that all three are required to understand production systems.\"}]\n33:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"This idea is outdated.\"}]\n34:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Metrics and traces are powerful in theory but brittle in practice. Instrumentation is complex and error-prone. Aggregations are confusing and often hide real problems. Flame graphs look sophisticated but are unintuitive for most people.\"}]\n35:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Logs are different.\"}]\n36:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Everyone knows how to write a log line. Everyone knows how to read stdout. Logs match how humans naturally reason about systems: what happened, in what order, and with what context.\"}]\n37:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"On a fundamental level, logs, metrics, and traces share the same underlying DNA: events. Metrics are aggregated events. Traces are collections of start and end events. Logs are events masquerading under a different name. The implications of this are profound: with logs, you can reconstruct metrics and traces, giving you three \\\"pillars\\\" for the price of one.\"}]\n38:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Historically, logs were dismissed because they were unstructured. Today, that weakness is a strength. AI excels at processing large volumes of unstructured text. It can surface patterns, identify anomalies, and extract meaning from natural language at scale. Metrics and traces could never hope to be as rich.\"}]\n39:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Logs have challenges, too. Cost and availability are chief among them. But these aren't insurmountable. Cost can be addressed with summarization, compression, tiering, and intelligent retention. Availability can be improved through automatic instrumentation: AI that adds meaningful log lines directly to code.\"}]\n3a:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"The Bitter Lesson taught us that AI progress doesn't come from clever hacks. It comes from simple, scalable primitives. A similar rule applies to observability platform.\"}]\n3b:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":[\"$\",\"strong\",null,{\"children\":\"Logs are all you need.\"}]}]\n3c:[\"$\",\"h2\",null,{\"id\":\"3-monitoring-is-dead\",\"children\":[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"#3-monitoring-is-dead\",\"className\":\"group block no-underline\",\"children\":[\"3. Monitoring is about detection: predefined thresholds on CPU, memory, or other signals. Observability is about understanding: the ability to explore systems and explain failures.\"}]\n3e:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Today, software teams think of monitoring as a necessary evil — a painful but essential part of running production systems. But this consensus doesn't change the truth: monitoring is fundamentally broken.\"}]\n3f:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Ask any engineer, and you'll hear the same complaints:\"}]\n40:[\"$\",\"ul\",null,{\"children\":[\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"Monitors are tedious to create and maintain.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"They require constant tuning.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"They misfire.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"They page the wrong people at the wrong time.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"Worst of all, they train teams to ignore alerts that sometimes represent real customer pain.\"}],\"\\n\"]}]\n41:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"These tradeoffs might be acceptable if monitors reliably caught issues. They don't.\"}]\n42:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Monitoring fails because it's reactive. Teams create monitors after incidents, not before. Meanwhile, the systems they manage are complex, constantly changing, and rarely fail the same way twice.\"}]\n43:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"We're playing a losing game. We don't need better monitors.
